- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

26	// RunOnce rebuilds the payload of all memos.
27	func (r *Runner) RunOnce(ctx context.Context) {
28		// Process memos in batches to avoid loading all memos into memory at once
29		const batchSize = 100
30		offset := 0
31		processed := 0
32

34			limit := batchSize
35			memos, err := r.Store.ListMemos(ctx, &store.FindMemo{

38			})

**Answer: `*markdown.service` (the single unexported struct, built by `markdown.NewService`) — constructed once in `NewAPIV1Service` — held by `APIV1Service`, `rss.RSSService`, and `memopayload.Runner`.**

### The interface
`internal/markdown/markdown.go:31` defines `markdown.Service` with eight methods: `ExtractAll`, `ExtractTags`, `ExtractProperties`, `RenderMarkdown`, `RenderHTML`, `GenerateSnippet`, `ValidateContent`, `RenameTag`.

### Concrete implementation — exactly one
`type service struct { md goldmark.Markdown }` at `internal/markdown/markdown.go:58` is the only implementation in the repo (`ExtractAll` has a single receiver: `internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`). There is no mock/fake/stub alternative — tests use the real thing.

It's a goldmark pipeline configured by functional options (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:85-113`): always GFM, plus optional `extensions.TagExtension` (`WithTagExtension`) and `extensions.MentionExtension` (`WithMentionExtension`). `RenderMarkdown`/`RenameTag` delegate to `renderer.NewMarkdownRenderer()` (`internal/markdown/renderer/markdown_renderer.go`); custom nodes live in `internal/markdown/ast/{tag,mention}.go` and `internal/markdown/parser/{tag,mention}.go`. So the runtime behavior varies by *options*, not by type.

### Construction
- **Production, the only runtime call site:** `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51` — `NewAPIV1Service` calls `markdown.NewService(markdown.WithTagExtension(), markdown.WithMentionExtension())` and stores it on the struct. `server/server.go:76` is what invokes `NewAPIV1Service`, then passes `apiV1Service.MarkdownService` into the RSS service at `server/server.go:85` — so RSS shares the *same instance*, not a second one.
- **Test-only constructions:** `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:48` (tags + mentions), `server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go:427` (tags only), `server/router/rss/rss_test.go:54` (no options — GFM only).

### Holders of the interface type
1. `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`. Used at `memo_service.go:108` and `:447` (payload rebuild on create/update), `memo_mention_helpers.go:32` (`ExtractAll`), `memo_service_webhooks.go:85` (`GenerateSnippet`, 64 chars).
2. `rss.RSSService.MarkdownService` — `server/router/rss/rss.go:45`, injected via `NewRSSService` (`rss.go:58`), used for `RenderHTML` at `rss.go:339` — the one server-side HTML render path (the frontend otherwise renders markdown itself, per the interface doc comment at `markdown.go:29-30`).
3. `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16`, injected via `NewRunner` (`runner.go:19`), used at `runner.go:52`.

One caveat worth flagging: **`memopayload.NewRunner` has no call site anywhere outside its own package** — `server/server.go` only wires `s3presign.NewRunner` (`server.go:162`). The `Runner` struct holds the interface but never actually executes; the live path into that package is the free function `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, markdownService)` (`runner.go:74`), which the API service calls directly with its own instance.
